# The problem to solve  {.Xsmaller}

- You have a task that can be _**automated with code**_

- You want to know how an _**AI assistant**_ can help 



# Why automation with code? {.smaller}

::: {.incremental}
- **Repetitive tasks** can be automated to _save time and reduce errors_
- **Scalability**: Automation allows _scaling out in parallel_ if needed
- **Scheduled tasks** can be automated to run at specific times _without human attention_
- **Judgment-based tasks** can be automated with _AI acting as your surrogate_
- **Complex tasks** can be automated by _building workflows incrementally_, with each step validated before moving on to the next
- **Reproducibility**: Automated workflows can be _reproduced exactly_, verified by others, and shared with others/the future self
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
<div style="text-align: center;">[[**Code enables**]{style="color:green;"} **knowledge accumulation and transfer**]{style="margin-top:0;"}</div>
:::



# Automation with code: Examples {.Xsmaller}

- **Structured/Unstructured data collection**, such as database queries, web scraping 
- **Summarization/Categorization** with large language models (LLMs) via API calls
- **Document/Image processing**, such as text extraction, color correction, watermarking



# No programming Experience? {.smaller}

::: {.incremental}
- _**"I don't know how to code!"**_ &emsp; ![Scared2Death]  
  - [**English**]{style="color:green;"} is the new programming language

- Your productivity is only limited by **how clear** 
  - you _**explain your problem**_ to AI
  - you _**specify your requirements**_ for the solution

- A capable AI assistant will fill in the gaps in between 
  - but you need to **guide** it with clear instructions and feedback
:::

# Why GitHub, GitHub Codespace, and GitHub Copilot? {.smaller}

::: {.incremental}
- **GitHub** provides spaces to _store, manage, and share code_ with others
  - Code files of a project are organized in a _**repository**_ (_**repo**_) with _**version control**_ to track changes

- GitHub **Codespace** (built on **VS Code**) provides a _**ready-to-use development environment**_ in the cloud,without requiring the setup of VS Code in a local machine

- GitHub **Copilot** is an _**AI assistant**_ sitting inside Codespace/VS Code to 
  - answer your questions (_**Ask**_ mode)
  - formulate plans to implement your ideas (_**Plan**_ mode)
  - act as your agent to execute the plans to generate code and verify the results (_**Agent**_ mode)
:::

# Why version control is important {.Xsmaller}

::: {.incremental}
- Version control (by **Git**) tracks changes to your code over time

- To **commit** changes (i.e., save them for the long term), you must give a _commit message_ to describe the changes made

- This sets a checkpoint that allows _**reverting to a previous version**_ of the code,
  - protecting you from losing the original work after _**failed experimentation**_ or accidental deletion by you or your **AI assistant**.
:::



# Branches of a repo on GitHub {.Xsmaller}

- **Main branch**: The default branch of a repo, where the _**stable version**_ of the code is stored

- **Feature/Development branch**: A branch created to develop a new feature or experiment with code changes, without affecting the main branch



# DS {.Xsmaller}

- _**Data science**_ (**DS**) is an interdisciplinary field that combines math, statistics, programming, and business knowledge to _**turn raw, messy data into useful insights**_. 

- Traditional DS courses provide systematic and [**comprehensive** coverage](https://www.udemy.com/course/python-core-and-advanced/) of a programming language (such as **Python** or R)
  - building knowledge firmly from the ground up

- _**Downside**_:
  - Buried into details, students can easily **lose the big picture**, 
    - forgetting why it is worth learning a DS programming language



# Our Strategy 

- _**One day is too short**_ for developing the knowledge comprehensively in the traditional manner
  
- Instead, this workshop simply 
  - showcases some <span style="color:green;">code examples with which students can _**modify and experiment**_</span> to turn them into _**their own projects**_ through learn by doing 
    - using _**AI as their <span style="color:green;">learning and research partner</span>**_



# Why Python? {.Xsmaller}

- Python has become the undisputed industry standard due to an  _**unmatched ecosystem of pre-built tools**_. 

- In late 1990s, the scientific and academic computing communities adopted Python for mathematics and research.

- As the "Big Data" and AI boom later took off, researchers naturally built their new machine learning tools on top of the Python code they already knew.

# The goal {.smaller}

- Is NOT to turn students into proficient coders

- Rather, the module aims to:

  - Inspire students to independently explore selected tools, driven by their **own interests and motivation**
  - Support students' **self-directed exploration** through signposting closely related resources

- These are achieved by 
  - sharing <span style="color:green;">code templates with which students can _**modify and experiment**_ to turn them into _**their own projects**_</span> through learn by doing
  - providing guidance through the signposting _**Read/Watch in Advance and After**_ documents



## Two weeks into the module ...

- You learned how to 
  - **automate** the **computation** and **visualization** of an important financial measure (Altman Z-Score) 
    - using **panel data** of S&P 500 firms fetched from Yahoo Finance 



## Four weeks into the module ...

- You learned how to 
  - **prepare and clean data** for analysis
  - conduct basic data analysis and present results with **interactive visualizations**
  - deploy a **dashboard app** and publish a **multi-tabbed webpage** to the world



## Week 5 Key takeaways

- _**AI is an integral part of your learning journey**_ 
  - _**for this module — and beyond**_
- Don't wait for others to help you. 
  - Engage in an _**active learning**_ journey assisted by AI to  
  _**<span style="color: green;">give yourself a brighter future!</span> **_



## Week 6 & 7 Key takeaways {.smaller}

- Data science provides tools and techniques for _web scraping_, _webcrawling_, and _natural language processing_ (NLP), 
  - allowing collecting and analyzing unstructured data with **minimal human intervention**

- The **<span style="color: green;">automation pipeline</span>** can handle large volumes of data efficiently  
(e.g., multiple years of the S&P 500 companies' unstructured data), 
  - **conserving** your time, energy, and attention **for more value-adding tasks** such as 
    - learning from each identified page with a high frequency of the matched keywords (e.g., water pollution)



## Week 8 & 9 Key takeaways

- LLMs are powerful tools for a variety of tasks 
  - but **hallucination** is a major risk
- Techniques such as _prompt engineering_ and _grounding_ can be used to 
  - guide LLMs towards more accurate and reliable outputs
- API access to LLMs enables the **automation** and **scalability** 
  - required for large volumes of **judgment-based** analysis tasks, such as financial sentiment analysis



## Week 10 Key takeaways  

- _**No single tool solves every problem**_
  - Use Python for AI/Machine Learning (ML) tasks, but leverage R for rigorous statistical modeling 
  - Selecting the "_**right tool for the job**_" is a key skill for data professionals

- The landscape of data science and AI **changes rapidly**
  - Continuous **self-learning and exploration** is the key to always choosing the right tool for the job

## Free computing platforms {.smaller}

- _GitHub Codespaces_ has **VS Code** as its GUI
  - native for Python and **GitHub Copilot**; can be set up for R too
  - provided by **GitHub**, a home for numerous _**open-source**_ codes

- _Posit cloud_ has **RStudio** as its GUI
  - mainly for R; can use **GitHub Copilot**

- Google _Colab_ has a **Jupyter notebook** GUI
  - native for Python and **Gemini** (AI assistant developed by Google)
  - (unspecified) **GPU access** for free-tier users

- _Lightning.ai_ has **VS Code** and **Jupyter Lab** as its GUIs
  - The VS Code interface has **GitHub Copilot** 
  - [35 hours**/month** free](https://lightning.ai/pricing)  **GPU access** 



## DS vs AI 

- _**Data science**_ (**DS**) and _**machine learning**_ (**ML**) provide key foundations for _**artificial intelligence**_ (**AI**)

  - ML is a core subfield of AI and underpins most modern AI systems.

  - DS supplies the data handling, statistical analysis, and modeling practices that make ML and AI practical and effective.



## The Answer 

[• You will not be replaced by AI]{.sp .fragment .fade-in-then-out}  

[• You will be replaced by someone who can **use AI better** &emsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &thinsp; **than you**]{.sp .fragment .fade-up}
